newsitem.title: USA: U S West Media, Airtouch in definitive deal.
newsitem.headline: U S West Media, Airtouch in definitive deal.

text.p: U S West Media Group and AirTouch Communications Inc. said Friday they reached a definitive agreement in the previously announced $5 billion merger of U S West's cellular telephone operations into AirTouch Communications Inc.

As part of the agreement, U S West will transfer its domestic directory business from U S West Media Group to U S West Communications Group. The two groups are separately traded entities that make up U S West, a Denver-based regional telephone company created by the breakup of AT&T in 1984.

U S West said the directory business, U S West Dex, is worth about $4.75 billion. The company said U S West Communications will pay $850 million in stock to U S West Media and assume $3.9 billion of the media group's debt in exchange for the directory business.

The communications group was set up in 1995 as a separately traded entity so that investors could track U S West's traditional telephone business. It provides telecommunications services in 14 Western and Midwestern states.
U S West Media Group has operations in domestic and international cable and telephone service, wireless communications and directory and information services.

AirTouch Communications, based in San Franciso, is a global wireless communications company, with interests in cellular, paging, and personal communications services in the United States, Europe and Asia.
U S West and Airtouch signed a letter of intent for the deal in April. The main terms of the definitive agreement are the same as those in the letter of intent, the companies said.
Under those terms, Airtouch would obtain U S West Media Group's domestic wireless business and U S West Media Group would obtain an equity stake in Airtouch.
The proposed merger is contingent upon the companies' obtaining tax free status for the sale of U S West's wireless operations to Airtouch.
The terms of the agreement call for U S West Media Group to issue between 84.8 million and 93.3 million shares to the media group, depending on Airtouch's share price.
The companies said if they fail to obtain tax-free status, they will continue with a joint operating agreement established in 1994.

U S West Media traded at $19.125, up 75 cents, in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Airtouch traded at $25.875, up 12.5 cents, and U S West Communications traded at $35.25, up 25 cents, also on the NYSE.
